_assumptions.text: npm audit could not be run: this repo has no lockfile and node_modules/ is absent by design, and npm audit requires a lockfile. No advisory ids were observed for express 4.17.1, sqlite3 5.0.2 or eslint 8.57.0, and none are claimed. Bootstrap to reproduce: `npm install --package-lock-only && npm audit --json --omit=dev`.

npm run lint could not be executed to confirm the eslint-config finding, because node_modules/ is absent and installing is forbidden. Bootstrap: `npm install && npm run lint`. The finding is recorded as inferred for that reason.

Branch protection and required-review settings were not assessed: no CODEOWNERS or ruleset config exists in tree, and these settings live in the forge rather than the repository, so they cannot be observed from source.

Scorecard checks whose premise is public open-source distribution - License, Security-Policy, Signed-Releases, Packaging, Fuzzing, CII-Best-Practices, Contributors - were deliberately not reported. package.json sets private true and README.md states this is a fixture, not a published package, so SLSA provenance and SBOM have no artifact to attach to either.
No containers, Dockerfile, compose file, or deploy manifests exist in this directory, so the container section of the doctrine had nothing to assess.
No .gitignore exists in this directory, but nothing untracked-and-sensitive is currently present, so it is recorded here rather than as a finding.

eslint is declared in devDependencies but node_modules/ is absent and no eslint config file exists, so lint could not be executed. Lint output was not consulted for any finding here; infra-supplychain owns the missing config.
The test suite was not run - tests-correctness owns it per doctrine.

The SQL injection in db.js and the credential fallback in client.js were observed while tracing the performance paths but are left to security-appsec; they appear above only as impact context for the unwired validators.
Table growth rate for the unbounded query is inferred from the POST route being unauthenticated; no load test was performed, so the specific row count at which the endpoint degrades is unknown.

Whether the deployment target is an orchestrator or load balancer could not be confirmed - no Dockerfile, compose file, or deployment manifest exists. The health/SIGTERM finding assumes the service is deployed behind one, which the README framing and the bare app.listen suggest but do not prove.

The personal-data inventory is inferred from code rather than from a schema: there is no CREATE TABLE anywhere in the repo, and saveProfile builds its column list dynamically, so the actual table shape is whatever a client last posted. Email, age and postcode are the fields the code demonstrably handles; there may be more.
Did not execute the service or observe a real log line or outbound request - node_modules/ is absent and no install was run. All findings are traced statically from source.

No retention configuration, log shipping target, or backup mechanism is present in the repo, so where the console.log stream ends up and how long it is kept could not be determined; the impact statement assumes typical stdout collection.
The geo API host is a placeholder domain; whether a real third party would receive this data in a deployed version of this fixture is unknowable from source.
node_modules/ is not installed and there is no lockfile, so no runtime exploitation was executed. Every injection finding was traced by reading source, not by sending a request.
Could not determine whether the geo key literal is live; the host is an RFC 2606 example domain, which suggests fixture data. The fail-open fallback pattern is the defect regardless.
express.json() applies express's default 100kb body cap, so no unbounded-body finding is reported.
log.js logs the full request body. That is privacy-data's slice, not reported here.
Authorization was not assessed: none of the three routes has auth middleware, but that is security-authz-identity's slice.
node_modules/ is not installed, so nothing was executed; all three findings were established by reading src/server.js and src/routes.js end to end rather than by sending a request.

The exact column set of the profiles table could not be confirmed - no schema or migration file exists - so the mass-assignment finding names id as the concrete settable column and does not assert that a role or admin column exists.

Out of slice, handed to security-appsec: the two unparameterized queries in src/db.js, the committed credential fallback and plaintext base URL in src/client.js. The empty catch in client.js belongs to performance-observability; the request-body logging in src/log.js to privacy-data.

No cookies, sessions, or tokens are set or read anywhere in the repo, so no CSRF, session-management (ASVS V7), or token-verification (ASVS V9) finding is reported - those controls are absent because the auth model itself is absent, which findings 1 and 2 already cover.

node_modules/ is absent and per doctrine I did not install it. The unit suite still executed because test/validate.test.js imports only src/validate.js, which has no third-party imports; the other src files import express and sqlite3 and were never loaded by any test run.
The unhandled-rejection outcome for listProfiles is traced from Node's default behavior on Node 24, not executed - the server cannot be started without express and sqlite3 installed.
No coverage instrumentation is configured and none was run, so no coverage numbers or thresholds are reported.
The corrected `node --test` invocation was run only to establish that the two existing assertions pass and that the failure is in the script, not the tests. No files were modified.
